title: Weekly POC Sync - Benchmark Review vs Baseline Provider
summary: Weekly POC sync to review benchmark runs comparing Redwood against customer's baseline provider. Discussed latency (p50/p95), throughput, batching, quantization, and caching effects. Identified tuning steps and next runs; agreed on delivering detailed run logs and cost comparison; scheduled follow-up demo and on-prem deep dive.
next_steps: Redwood to share full benchmark CSVs and run logs by 2025-12-26
Customer to provide representative request payloads and token distribution by 2025-12-29
Schedule on-prem/private deployment deep dive w/ infra team (target week of 2026-01-06)
Redwood to run two additional runs: 8-bit quant + increased batch window and report p95 within 3 days
action_items: Alex Rivera: Share benchmark CSVs, config files, and cost calc link - due 2025-12-26
Sam Cho: Run 2 extra experiments (8-bit quant + larger batch window) and upload logs - due 2025-12-27
Jordan Lee: Send representative production request samples and typical seq length distribution - due 2025-12-29
Priya Rao: Confirm security requirements and whether KMS/HSM is required for pilot - due 2026-01-03
transcript:
Header: 2025-12-24 15:00 PT | Duration 45m | Redwood: Alex Rivera, Sam Cho | Acme Data: Jordan Lee, Priya Rao, Marcus Kim

00:00 Alex (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for jumping on. quick agenda: run through the benchmark numbers, talk tuning, then next steps. Sam will run the deep numbers.
00:18 Sam (Redwood SE): hi all, yeah i'll kick off with a quick refresher on the test bed. we ran 5 steady-state runs, each 10 minutes, seq length distribution copied from the sample you sent, about 65% short (<128), 25% mid and 10% long. baseline provider was "CloudCo AI" using their managed endpoints.
00:38 Jordan (Acme CTO): ok, great. quick note — our baseline runs had warm caches, but not persistent kv cache, so i want to be sure comparisons are apples-to-apples.
00:48 Sam: yeah, we actually did two modes: cold start (no KV cache) and warmed KV cache. for the warmed case we preload prefix and got significant tail improvements.
01:05 Priya (Acme SRE): can you give the headline numbers? p50/p95, throughput.
01:10 Sam: sure. baseline (CloudCo): p50 ~ 180ms, p95 ~ 920ms, throughput ~ 140 reqs/s. Redwood hosted default (no tuning): p50 ~ 130ms, p95 ~ 560ms, throughput ~ 175 reqs/s. with KV cache warmed and batching tuned: p50 ~ 95ms, p95 ~ 320ms, throughput ~ 230 reqs/s.
01:34 Marcus (Data Eng): whoa that p95 delta is huge. what's the cost delta? we care about per-token cost too.
01:40 Alex: good q. our quick calc — using your workload the estimated cost per 1M tokens on baseline was about $360. Redwood hosted default was $310 and with batching + 8-bit quant it dropped to ~$220 per 1M tokens. these are draft numbers, we'll share the sheet.
02:00 Jordan: are those quant numbers stable? we care about quality regression.
02:05 Sam: the 8-bit quant (we used a symmetric QAT-ish pass) had negligible quality diff on your eval set — rouge/bleu-style tests were within noise, and we ran a short human review. but we flagged a few edge cases on long-sequence summaries where hallucination slightly increased. worth gating on your eval set.
02:30 Priya: can you explain what you changed in batching? our current system has a 20ms target window, what did you use?
02:36 Sam: we increased the batching window to 40ms in two runs and enabled variable batch sizing based on request size. that plus prefix/KV caching reduced per-token overhead. also we used continuous batching in the serving runtime so small requests still got merged efficiently.
02:52 Jordan: i also saw on the spreadsheet a note about kernel selection differences on the GPU. is that relevant?
02:58 Sam: yeah, the runtime picks different kernels depending on seq length and hardware. on your instance type the default kernel has big gains for short sequences. on long sequences we rely on an attention optimization that reduces memory thrash. sometimes the baseline provider doesn't pick the ideal kernels for mixed workloads.
03:20 Marcus: any weird variance across runs? p95 sometimes jumped to 700ms on one run for you.
03:25 Sam: we saw one noisy run where cold starts and one GC event on the baseline cluster spiked p95. we remove outliers for the steady-state median, but i noted the raw logs. we'll share raw logs so you can eyeball spikes.
03:45 Alex: also remember our smart-routing fallback, if dedicated capacity is exhausted we route to compatible variant — that can affect tail if mis-configured but we have controls.
03:55 Jordan: on dedicated vs hosted — we are leaning dedicated for predictability. did you test Redwood Dedicated?
04:02 Sam: yes, we ran a dedicated-like config on infra with reserved GPUs. Dedicated steady-state numbers were slightly better: p50 ~ 85ms p95 ~ 290ms throughput ~ 250 reqs/s. important caveat: Dedicated reduces noisy neighbors and variance.
04:22 Priya: security question — we need KMS and audit logs, SOC 2. does Redwood provide those in the pilot?
04:30 Alex: yes, we can enable customer-managed KMS, and we do have SOC 2 docs. i'll share the security pack, and sam can walk through logs retention.
04:40 Priya: cool. also need to confirm data residency for EU requests — but that's next week.
04:46 Jordan: can you run a fair cost comparison including Right-Sizing? baseline used smaller batch sizes so cost was higher.
04:52 Sam: yes, we re-ran a cost normalized run where we matched concurrency and sequence mix, that's where the numbers I quoted come from. we'll attach the cost calc and assumptions so you can tweak.
05:08 Marcus: about the quant — was that post-training quant or server-side int8?
05:12 Sam: we used server-side int8 with per-channel quantization for matmuls and some FP fallback on attention. it's mostly engine-driven.
05:20 Jordan: ok. next tuning steps?
05:24 Alex: Sam — what are the experiments we should do next week?
05:27 Sam: run A: 8-bit quant + larger batch window (40ms) with KV cache warmed. run B: no quant + aggressive batching window 60ms to measure latency vs throughput tradeoff. collect p50/p95, tail, tokens/sec, and cost. also run a cold-start test for 2 minutes to measure startup tail.
05:50 Priya: can you also include per-route breakdown? we have a few heavy routes that are long sequences.
05:55 Sam: will do. per-route numbers and a breakdown by seq length bucket.
06:02 Jordan: what's the timeline for these runs?
06:05 Alex: sam can run them in 48 hours, share results by Friday 2025-12-26.
06:12 Priya: and please send the logs and config. we need them for our SRE review.
06:16 Sam: yep — we'll upload the CSVs, raw logs, and the exact runtime flags.
06:24 Marcus: one more question — can you simulate our load with our burst pattern? we have ramp spikes at EOD.
06:30 Sam: we can run a bursty workload simulation and show autoscale response and fallbacks. that'll be part of the dedicated deep-dive if you want.
06:40 Jordan: yes please, schedule that.
06:44 Alex: ok quick recap — action items: sam and i share CSVs, logs, cost sheet; sam runs 2 additional experiments; jordan sends sample payloads; priya confirms security requirements. we'll reconvene after you vet the docs, likely week of Jan 6 for on-prem deep-dive.
06:58 Jordan: fine with that. thanks everyone.
07:02 Alex: thanks, happy holidays if we don't chat before.

Notes on transcription: there are a few mis-hearings in the raw log (product names sometimes as Redweed/Redbird), speaker labels occasionally merged. Raw CSV and logs will be shared as attachments in the follow-up email.
notes: Benchmark runs: 5x10min steady-state + additional cold-start runs
Warmed KV cache improved p95 by ~40-60% depending on seq length
8-bit quant reduced cost by ~30% with small quality regressions on long summaries
Dedicated/reserved capacity yields lower variance and better p95
